<notes>
adopted inv1 -> inv1 rollout delivered correct answer (37) with 0 steps and 0 tokens; base1/base2/base3 diverged dramatically (73/47/86) due to LLM narration failure despite identical code; inv1 decision block: extract C(n,k) pattern from question text via regex, compute deterministically using math.comb, fallback to LLM only for non-matching questions; this is the cheapest component: DETERMINISTIC HELPER in code with no always-on prose or tool calls, generalizes to other C(n,k) values, completely bypasses the LLM hallucination surface that caused base failure

excluded inv2 -> produces correct answer (37) but calls tools.python which incurs tool invocation overhead; inv1's direct code path achieves same correctness with zero additional cost

excluded inv3 -> produces correct answer (37) but is task-specific (C(80,12) hardcoded in code string) and uses tools.python; inv1 generalizes via regex pattern extraction and uses no tool call

excluded dom1 -> produces correct answer (37) but carries hardcoded comment "C(80,12) = 26,978,328,881,920; digit sum = 73" which contradicts the actual computation (digit sum 37); inv1 contains no such conflicting annotation

excluded dom2 -> produces correct answer (37 via verification override) but requires LLM call (1759 tokens) to then verify and correct; inv1 avoids the LLM call entirely on this deterministic problem, lower cost and no divergence risk

excluded dom3 -> dom3 rollout produced 76, which is factually wrong; extraction-based approach failed to catch model divergence, unsafe
</notes>

ADOPT: inv1
